rationale: All reported cohorts with biallelic GTF3C3 variants universally present with intellectual disability, developmental delay, and neurological impairment, firmly supporting normal neurodevelopment as a robust negative predictor. However, regarding neuroimaging, while primary cohorts (Abdel-Hamid et al., De Hayr et al., López et al.) report cerebellar atrophy, corpus callosum abnormalities, and frontal hypoplasia across their cohorts, an earlier report of a patient with a GTF3C3 variant and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy noted that cerebral MRI showed no structural anomalies. Therefore, while normal neurodevelopment strongly argues against NEDFABS, the assertion that normal brain MRI conclusively rules out the diagnosis remains conflicted.

evidence.text: Four individuals from three families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants displayed developmental delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly, and brain imaging abnormalities including brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and frontal lobe hypoplasia.

source.quote: The patients exhibited microcephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability and distinctive dysmorphic facies that appear recognizable in very young children. new_directions.question_text: Does neuroimaging in GTF3C3-related disorder progress from normal in early infancy to progressive cerebellar/cerebral atrophy with age?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the absent MRI findings in young epileptic encephalopathy patients represent an early pre-atrophic stage or true phenotypic variability will refine the negative predictive value of brain MRI.

new_directions.question_text: Which facial dysmorphisms and neurodevelopmental trajectories distinguish NEDFABS from Pol III-related leukodystrophies (POLR3A/POLR3B) and other TFIIIC-related conditions?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative deep phenotyping across Pol III transcription-complex disorders will allow clinicians to distinguish GTF3C3-specific clinical hallmarks from overlapping encephalopathies.
